washington-first-inauguration.research_focus: the 1789 inauguration on the balcony of Federal Hall, Wall Street, New York, and its period depictions
washington-first-inauguration.scene: A tall man in a plain broadcloth suit stands on a columned balcony with his hand on a Bible held on a cushion, a packed street of tricorn hats below; seen from the side, face not the focus

john-adams-inauguration.research_focus: Congress Hall in Philadelphia and the 1797 inauguration of John Adams, the first peaceful handover between presidents
john-adams-inauguration.scene: Inside a modest brick legislative chamber, a short stout man in a dark suit takes the oath while a tall older man in a frock coat watches from the side, rows of seated congressmen in powdered wigs

jefferson-first-inauguration.research_focus: the unfinished Capitol in the new city of Washington in 1801 and Jefferson's plain walk to his swearing-in
jefferson-first-inauguration.scene: A tall man in an unadorned suit walks on foot across a muddy clearing toward a half-built stone Capitol wing with scaffolding, a few townsfolk following; no carriage, no grand procession

madison-first-inauguration.research_focus: the 1809 inauguration of James Madison in the House chamber and his suit of American-made merino wool
madison-first-inauguration.scene: A slight, small man in a dark homespun wool suit takes the oath in a domed legislative chamber, a lady in an empire-waist gown and turban watching from the gallery

monroe-first-inauguration.research_focus: the 1817 inauguration of James Monroe on an outdoor platform before the Old Brick Capitol
monroe-first-inauguration.scene: The first outdoor oath: a man in an old-fashioned knee-breeches suit stands on a raised wooden platform before a plain brick building, a crowd of thousands filling the open ground under a clear sky

john-quincy-adams-inauguration.research_focus: the 1825 inauguration of John Quincy Adams in the House chamber and the contested election decided by the House
john-quincy-adams-inauguration.scene: A balding man in a frock coat takes the oath on a law book rather than a Bible, in a grand semicircular chamber of marble columns and a draped canopy, the galleries crowded

jackson-first-inauguration.research_focus: the 1829 White House reception after Andrew Jackson's inauguration, when the crowd overran the mansion
jackson-first-inauguration.scene: A rowdy crowd of frontiersmen and townsfolk crams an elegant reception room, standing on upholstered chairs, a punch bowl tipped, china smashed on the floor, people climbing out through the windows

william-henry-harrison-inauguration.research_focus: the cold, wet inauguration of William Henry Harrison in March 1841 and his very long speech without a coat or hat
william-henry-harrison-inauguration.scene: An elderly man without hat or overcoat reads a very long speech from a sheaf of papers on the Capitol steps in sleet and wind, the bundled-up crowd stamping their feet

polk-inauguration.research_focus: the rain-soaked 1845 inauguration of James K. Polk and the new telegraph line that carried news of it
polk-inauguration.scene: A brass telegraph key and paper-tape register on a wooden desk by a rain-streaked window; outside, a sea of umbrellas below the Capitol steps where a distant small figure takes the oath

lincoln-first-inauguration.research_focus: Lincoln's 1861 inauguration at the Capitol with its unfinished dome, under heavy guard, and the Civil War's approach
lincoln-first-inauguration.scene: A tall bearded man in a frock coat speaks from a wooden platform before the Capitol, its dome still a skeleton of iron and cranes, soldiers with rifles posted on rooftops and along the crowd

grant-first-inauguration.research_focus: Ulysses S. Grant's 1869 inauguration and the Union army veterans who marched in his parade
grant-first-inauguration.scene: A short bearded man in a plain dark civilian suit stands at the Capitol with his hand raised, while columns of Union veterans in army greatcoats march past below with regimental flags

cleveland-first-inauguration.research_focus: Grover Cleveland's 1885 inauguration and the Democratic crowds celebrating their first presidency since before the Civil War
cleveland-first-inauguration.scene: A large moustached man in a frock coat takes the oath on the Capitol's east portico under its finished dome, a festive crowd below waving hats and bunting on every building

mckinley-first-inauguration.research_focus: William McKinley's 1897 inauguration and the early motion picture cameras that filmed it
mckinley-first-inauguration.scene: A hand-cranked wooden motion picture camera on a tripod in the foreground, its operator turning the crank, aimed at a distant ceremony on the Capitol steps where a figure stands with raised hand

theodore-roosevelt-sworn-in.research_focus: the Ansley Wilcox House in Buffalo where Theodore Roosevelt took the oath in September 1901 after McKinley's death
theodore-roosevelt-sworn-in.scene: In a book-lined library of a private house, a sturdy man with spectacles and moustache stands with right hand raised before a small group of sombre men in dark suits; a quiet, hurried scene, not a ceremony

taft-inauguration.research_focus: the 1909 blizzard that forced William Howard Taft's inauguration indoors into the Senate chamber
taft-inauguration.scene: Heavy snow buries the Capitol plaza and the empty outdoor stand, workers shovelling drifts; through a tall window, a warmly lit Senate chamber where a very large man takes the oath

wilson-first-inauguration.research_focus: the March 1913 Woman Suffrage Procession down Pennsylvania Avenue the day before Woodrow Wilson's inauguration
wilson-first-inauguration.scene: A long procession of women in long coats and wide hats marches down a broad avenue toward the Capitol dome, a woman on horseback leading in a cape, crowds pressing in from both sides; no lettering on banners

harding-inauguration.research_focus: the electric loudspeaker system first used at the 1921 inauguration on the Capitol's east portico
harding-inauguration.scene: Large horn-shaped loudspeakers mounted on poles above a vast hatted crowd before the Capitol, a single microphone on a stand at the empty railing; no recognisable person

hoover-inauguration.research_focus: the rainy 1929 inauguration and the stock market prosperity that collapsed later that year
hoover-inauguration.scene: A sodden reviewing stand draped in bunting stands empty in the rain below the Capitol, umbrellas everywhere, while a ticker-tape machine in the foreground spills curling paper tape; no recognisable person

fdr-first-inauguration.research_focus: the March 1933 inauguration during the Great Depression and its broadcast to the nation by radio
fdr-first-inauguration.scene: A family in worn clothes gathers close around a wooden cathedral radio in a bare kitchen, listening intently to the inaugural speech, a closed bank's shuttered doors visible through the window

truman-sworn-in.research_focus: the Cabinet Room of the White House on 12 April 1945, where the new president was sworn in hours after Roosevelt's death
truman-sworn-in.scene: A long polished cabinet table in a quiet panelled room in the evening, a Bible laid on it, a clock on the mantel and a portrait above; empty chairs pushed back, no recognisable person

eisenhower-first-inauguration.research_focus: the 1953 inauguration and parade, with military bands and a general-turned-president
eisenhower-first-inauguration.scene: Military bands and marching columns pass a reviewing stand on Pennsylvania Avenue in winter sun, an army five-star general's cap resting on the stand's rail; no recognisable person

kennedy-inauguration.research_focus: the snowy, bitterly cold 20 January 1961 inauguration on the Capitol's east front
kennedy-inauguration.scene: Fresh snow banks the Capitol plaza under a bright winter sky, the inaugural stand crowded with spectators in heavy coats and fur hats seen from behind, their breath visible; no recognisable person

lbj-sworn-in-air-force-one.research_focus: the exterior of the presidential Boeing 707, SAM 26000, parked at Love Field, Dallas, on 22 November 1963
lbj-sworn-in-air-force-one.scene: A long four-engined jet airliner parked on a hot Texas airfield, boarding stairs at its rear door, a cluster of dark cars and grim-faced security men at its foot; no recognisable person

nixon-first-inauguration.research_focus: the January 1969 inauguration in Washington and the anti-war protesters along the parade route
nixon-first-inauguration.scene: A bleak winter avenue lined by police, the inaugural parade's limousines passing at a distance, while protesters in the foreground hold up peace-symbol placards with no lettering; no recognisable person

carter-inauguration.research_focus: the 1977 inaugural parade when the new president walked down Pennsylvania Avenue instead of riding
carter-inauguration.scene: An empty presidential limousine rolls slowly down a broad cold avenue toward the White House, its back seat vacant, as a cheering crowd turns to watch walkers ahead; a basket of peanuts on a spectator's lap; no recognisable person

reagan-first-inauguration.research_focus: the first inauguration held on the Capitol's west front in 1981, and the release of the American hostages in Iran the same day
reagan-first-inauguration.scene: Split by a tall window: outside, the inaugural stand on the Capitol's west front looking down the Mall; inside, a television showing a jetliner on a runway at dawn; ribbons tied around a tree; no recognisable person

george-hw-bush-inauguration.research_focus: the 1989 inauguration on the west front of the Capitol and the bicentennial of Washington's first inauguration
george-hw-bush-inauguration.scene: The Capitol's west front dressed in swags of bunting and flags for an inauguration, a lectern with the presidential seal on the stand and a Bible resting on it, crowds stretching down the Mall; no recognisable person

clinton-first-inauguration.research_focus: the 1993 inauguration, including the reading of the poem On the Pulse of Morning on the inaugural stand
clinton-first-inauguration.scene: From behind and high on the Capitol's west front, the inaugural stand looks out over a vast crowd along the Mall toward the Washington Monument on a clear winter day; a saxophone rests on a chair; no recognisable person

george-w-bush-first-inauguration.research_focus: the rainy, cold 2001 inauguration after the contested Florida recount and Supreme Court decision
george-w-bush-first-inauguration.scene: Rain falls on a sea of umbrellas along the Mall before the Capitol's west front, while in the foreground a stack of punched paper ballots and a magnifying glass sit on a table; no recognisable person
